findings.evidence: “This skill is a Process ... executed with Tool-level rigor” names rubric categories without helping the agent make a wizard decision. The surrounding instructions are overwhelmingly ai-kit-specific.
findings.fix: Lead with the actual rule: run steps 0–4 in order and use the ai-kit-spec.py factory subcommands to prevent quoting and model-ID mistakes. Record removal of the rubric labels only.

findings.evidence: “Only when HERDR_ENV=1 and the owner chose copilot as a preferred runtime” appears in Step 1.5, but the owner first chooses preferred runtimes in Step 2.2. On a first run the condition cannot be evaluated at its documented step.
findings.fix: Keep the initial catalog build in Step 1.5. Put the Copilot discovery decision, its explicit permission gate and its skip fallback in wizard-flow.md step 2, after runtime selection and before ranking.

findings.evidence: “Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup” is specific, but does not cue common requests to check availability or stale providers without saying “setup,” or distinguish configuration from running an already configured review or execute lane.
findings.fix: Use this skill to set up or refresh ai-kit cross-AI review and execution lanes, even if the user only asks which models should review plans, which CLI should implement them, or what should run first or as a fallback. Detect installed CLIs, propose separate review and execute sets from the model catalog, and ask the owner to confirm picks, effort, order and opt-ins. Write [lanes] in .aikit/config.toml by default; announce the exact path and ask before replacing any roster. --local and --global choose the target, not replacement consent. Use --check-only to report availability and stale providers without persisting ai-kit state. For an old review-spec.toml, explain pending migration or handle it during approved replacement. Also use when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers setup because no lanes exist. Not for running configured lanes or editing unrelated config.toml tables.

findings.evidence: “Build the JSON shape ... render-toml ... expects” starts a dense inline schema that overlaps the existing reference example. The 461-line body has about 6,650 words before tokenization, well above the recommended 5,000 tokens despite good branch-specific reference triggers.
findings.fix: Keep the target, replacement gate, exact write command and exit checks in Step 3. Move its full field-by-field assembly rules into references/config-file.md beside the JSON example, and explicitly load that section only on the write branch. Preserve every role, effort, consent and evidence requirement.

findings.evidence: “--global forces <user config> directly” and “--local also forces local directly” both skip scope selection. When both flags are passed, there is no rule for deciding which file is meant.
findings.fix: Make --local and --global mutually exclusive. If both are passed, stop before any setup write and ask the owner to choose one; neither flag grants replacement consent.

findings.evidence: “If the proposal shows an alias group” lets the alias eval pass when the group is missing. The input is a Markdown excerpt, not a seeded roster and model catalog that guarantee a qualifying alias is returned.
findings.fix: Seed the roster, runtime and catalog for the alias case, then require the exact alias to appear under aliases and assert that it has no rank or score and triggers no heuristic question.

findings.evidence: “Write my reviewer config to the global review-spec file” treats the retired file as a write destination. The 10/10 set otherwise has useful near-misses, but some negatives, such as “Write a unit test for the parser in the markdown-to-pdf skill,” do not test a boundary.
findings.fix: Use the current global ai-kit config.toml in the global-write query and retain the separate legacy-migration query. Replace an unrelated negative with a request to inspect or change only [skills.roles] without setting up lanes.

findings.evidence: “single seats the first available lane of the review order” contradicts quota.py:139–141 and 192–193. With an available same-vendor lane first and an available different-vendor lane second, single mode picks the second lane.
findings.fix: Explain that single mode follows the ladder while preferring a reviewer from a different vendor than the author, falling back to the first available same-vendor lane if needed. Explain that double mode takes the first available primary and only adds an independent secondary when one is available.

findings.evidence: “Run Step 2.5's ... test call for every chosen lane ... and a custom entry” lets an execute-only custom command pass check-reviewer and be saved as usable. quota.py:250–256 probes the review invocation; routing.py:138–141 returns no_formula for a custom command in execute mode.
findings.fix: Tell the owner that a successful check-reviewer call verifies only the review invocation. For a custom execute choice, surface no_formula before confirmation and offer a supported execute runtime or the session default instead.

findings.evidence: “Confirm the trusted bytes are the approved ones” compares only key/argv or key/error from a flattened preview. An execute entry hidden behind a duplicate review key can change without changing those lines; the extra check compares command text but not every field covered by the trust digest.
findings.fix: Have the preview return the canonical digest covering both roles and require that exact digest in the trusting call. Refuse before recording trust on any mismatch, then preview and ask again. Until the CLI supports that check, do not claim the preview comparison proves which bytes were approved.

findings.evidence: “On exit 2 with model catalog is empty, return to Step 1.5” has no terminal case when catalog.md forbids fetching to protect an unapproved legacy roster. An existing but empty catalog and owner answers of only auto leave the build skipped and the same proposal failure on every retry.
findings.fix: Carry the no-fetch decision into the proposal step. If no usable catalog entries remain, do not retry discovery: offer session-default-only setup when feasible, or stop and name the migration approval needed to proceed.

findings.evidence: “When its list differs ... (an added key, or another runtime, model or command for a key)” compares only fields printed by the preview. The quota launcher also fills custom-command placeholders from other flat lane fields, so a changed argument can leave the preview unchanged but alter the approved invocation.
findings.fix: Preview the resolved argv and include its inputs in a consent fingerprint. Have probe-quota check that fingerprint against the same resolved snapshot it will spawn, and abort on a mismatch rather than probing against a separately resolved roster.

findings.evidence: “its sonnet, opus, haiku and fable aliases” is presented as a fixed host fact without a source or check date. Anthropic documents additional aliases; the four named here are ai-kit's accepted native selectors, not the vendor's whole alias list.
findings.fix: Name the four as ai-kit's supported native selectors and use the detected Claude aliases field as the source for the choice. If documenting Claude Code's own alias coverage separately, cite its official model configuration page and the date checked.
